pairs.question: Is a quo fundus petitus erat ab alio eiusdem fundi nomine conventus est: si alterutri eorum iussu iudicis fundum restituisset et postea secundum alterum petitorem res iudicaretur, quemadmodum non duplex damnum traheret?
pairs.answer: Uter prior iudex iudicaret, eum oportere ita fundum petitori restitui iubere, ut possessori caveret vel satisdaret, si alter fundum evicisset, eum praestare.
pairs.derivation: Indirect-question consultation answered by a jurist. Dropped the framing word 'quaerebatur,' that introduces the question and 'respondi,' that introduces the answer; both narrate the exchange. The setup ('Is a quo fundus petitus erat... conventus est') is kept verbatim so the conditional and 'eorum' have a referent. Question normalized to terminal '?'. Answer runs to the single full stop closing the section; no interior trimming needed.

pairs.question: A quo servus petebatur et eiusdem servi nomine cum eo furti agebatur, si utroque iudicio condemnatus esset, quid se facere oporteret?
pairs.answer: Si prius servus ab eo evictus esset, non oportere iudicem cogere, ut eum traderet, nisi ei satisdatum esset, quod pro eo homine iudicium accepisset, si quid ob eam rem datum esset, id recte praestari.
pairs.derivation: Consultation ('quid se facere oporteret') answered by the jurist. Dropped the framing 'quaerebat,' before the question and the framing 'respondit,' embedded in the answer (between 'evictus esset,' and 'non oportere'); the surrounding words are contiguous source utterance. Setup kept so 'utroque iudicio' has its two suits as referent. Answer ends at the first full stop ('...id recte praestari.'); the following alternative branch ('sed si prius de furto iudicium...') is elaboration of a different case and is cut.

pairs.question: Habitator in aliena aedificia fenestras et ostia imposuit, eadem post annum dominus aedificiorum dempsit: is qui imposuerat possetne ea vindicare?
pairs.derivation: Real interrogative ('possetne') answered directly. Dropped the framing 'quaero,' and 'respondit'. Setup (the fitting and removal of windows/doors) kept verbatim so 'is qui imposuerat' and 'ea' have referents. Answer is the operative reply 'posse'; the continuation after the colon ('nam quae alienis aedificiis conexa essent...') is the supporting reasoning and is cut. Normalized 'posse' to capitalized 'Posse.'

pairs.question: Si quis navem suam aliena materia refecisset, num nihilo minus eiusdem navis maneret?
pairs.derivation: Reported question ('interrogatus... num... maneret') answered directly. Dropped the framing 'Minicius interrogatus,' and 'respondit'. The conditional setup is part of the question itself and is kept contiguous. Answer is the operative 'manere'; the following remark ('sed si in aedificanda ea idem fecisset, non posse iulianus notat...') is a separate case and is cut. Normalized to 'Manere.'

pairs.question: A tutore pupilli domum mercatus ad eius refectionem fabrum induxit: is pecuniam invenit: ad quem pertineat?
pairs.answer: Si non thensauri fuerunt, sed pecunia forte perdita vel per errorem ab eo ad quem pertinebat non ablata, nihilo minus eius eam esse, cuius fuerat.
pairs.derivation: Real interrogative ('ad quem pertineat') answered by the jurist. Dropped the framing 'quaeritur' before the question and 'respondi,' before the answer. Setup (buying the house, bringing in the workman who finds money) kept verbatim so 'is pecuniam invenit' and the referent of the money are intelligible. Answer runs to the single closing full stop; no trimming needed.
